pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: GVN's place simplification flattened dereferences through a pointee projection containing ProjectionElem::Index, even though the Index local (SSA) is not guaranteed to still hold the same value at the current location as when the pointee was borrowed. The fix gates project_deeper on the pointee projection containing no Index elements, preventing references to non-existing locals and stale index values.
analysis.originalLogic: In GVN's simplify_place_value, when simplifying a deref place, the pass simplified the pointee and then unconditionally flattened the remaining projection: it set `value = v;` and `place_ref = pointee.project_deeper(&place.projection[index..], self.tcx).as_ref();`. A second path did the same with `pointee.project_deeper(&[], self.tcx).as_ref();`. This assumed projecting the already-resolved pointee place deeper was always sound.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong rewrite was to call `pointee.project_deeper(&place.projection[index..], self.tcx)` (or `project_deeper(&[], ...)`) regardless of the pointee's projection contents. When `pointee.projection` contained `ProjectionElem::Index(_)`, this flattened the dereference through an index local, producing a place that references a local which may not be live/valid at the current location (the PR test comment calls this "references to non-existing locals"). The corrected behavior only performs `project_deeper` if `pointee.projection.iter().all(|elem| !matches!(elem, ProjectionElem::Index(_)))`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR places for dereferences of references produced by indexed projections, e.g. `let a = &array[i];` followed by use of `*a`, where `i` is computed in a temporary/SSA local. This covers array/slice indexing projections, with both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR forms.
analysis.trigger: GVN simplifies a deref place whose resolved pointee is a `Place` whose projection contains `ProjectionElem::Index(_)`.
preconditions: The pointee place's projection contains ProjectionElem::Index(_).
The index operand is a Local whose value is not guaranteed at the current location to equal its value where the pointee was borrowed.
GVN is simplifying the deref place (simplify_place_value) and would otherwise flatten via project_deeper.
pitfalls: Being an SSA local does not by itself make an Index operand usable at an arbitrary later location; its live/value validity must be guaranteed.
Do not conflate borrow/liveness restrictions with unrelated post-copy overwrite conditions; the specific hazard is the Index local inside the pointee projection.
Flattening through ProjectionElem::Index can create places referring to non-existing locals or use stale index values.

The MIR diff's retained test name or old comments do not indicate a replacement pass is wrong; compare actual value assignments (the fixed output uses `Add(copy _2, const 1_usize)` and `_3 = &_1[_4]`, not a fresh indexed temporary).
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt GVN regression test `dereference_indexing(array: [u8; 2], index: usize)` that computes `let i = index + 1;` then borrows `&array[i]` and reads through it with an `opaque` use to keep the code alive. Use CHECK lines to require `[[i]] = Add(copy _2, const 1_usize);` and `[[a]] = &_1[[[i]]];`, then `CHECK-NOT: [{{.*}}]` before `[[tmp:_.*]] = copy (*[[a]]);` to ensure no leftover index projection. Emit both `gvn.dereference_indexing.GVN.panic-abort.diff` and `gvn.dereference_indexing.GVN.panic-unwind.diff`, and call the function from `main` with `dereference_indexing([129, 14], 5);`.
evidence: GVN:  Do not flatten derefs with ProjectionElem::Index.
This should fix the bug you found with https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/131650
